newsitem.title: USA: Trinova to exit interior auto plastics.
newsitem.headline: Trinova to exit interior auto plastics.

text.p: Trinova Corp Thursday said it planned to completely exit its interior automotive plastics business and as a result expects to take a special charge in 1997 of not more than $30 million pretax or about $18.5 million after tax, or $0.61 per share.
The company said that fluid connectors, a core business of its Aeroquip unit, will continue to be its primary automotive focus.

Aeroquip's automotive fluid connectors -- hose and the attached fittings -- are used for conveying fluids in air conditioning, power steering and oil cooling systems in cars, light trucks, vans and sport utility vehicles.

Trinova said buyers are being sought for each of Aeroquip's interior automotive plastics operations. While the company is currently in negotiations with potential buyers, no agreements have been finalized, it said. Sales volume in 1996 for the facilities was about $130 million.
"They are all fine facilities with excellent work forces, but they are not central to our strategy for long-term growth," said Darryl Allen, Trinova chairman, president and chief executive officer.

"Customers for interior automotive components have been moving to large integrated suppliers, companies that are first-tier systems suppliers, rather than discreet component manufacturers. Our plastics facilities can fit well with manufacturers that have interior plastics as a focus. We intend to be out of the interior automotive plastics business by the end of the 1997 third quarter."
